title: Does a fan make air colder?
hook: A fan blows across a warm surface.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: The faster flow removes warm air next to the surface and increases convective heat transfer. A fan can cool a person without lowering the room's air temperature.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: The faster flow removes warm air next to the surface and increases convective heat transfer. A fan can cool a person without lowering the room's air temperature.

claims.text: The faster flow removes warm air next to the surface and increases convective heat transfer. A fan can cool a person without lowering the room's air temperature. Illustrative heat-flow values; actual cooling depends on airflow, humidity, temperatures, and evaporation. A running fan also adds its own electrical energy as heat.
claims.source: Convective heat-transfer model Q-dot = h A (T_surface − T_air); increased airflow can increase h while air temperature remains fixed. 20 W and 60 W are hypothetical.

recall.question: A fan blows air at unchanged room temperature across a warm mug. Which may increase?
recall.why: Moving air can increase convection without changing the incoming air temperature.
